title: Evaluate all six Well-Architected pillars
explanation:
Operational excellence concerns running and improving workloads through procedures, observability, controlled change and incident learning. Security concerns identities, infrastructure and data protection. Reliability concerns correct operation through disruption and recovery. Performance efficiency concerns selecting resources for workload needs. Cost optimization concerns useful outcomes without unnecessary spending. Sustainability concerns reducing environmental impact. These perspectives overlap, so the framework is not a contest to maximize one metric. Redundancy may add cost while satisfying a recovery requirement. An oversized fleet may waste money and energy without helping users. Review a specific workload against measurable goals, prioritize risks and validate improvements with evidence rather than placing six labels on an untested diagram.

Reliability and security are different requirements even when one failure affects both. Cost optimization does not mean choosing the lowest hourly price regardless of service requirements.

Worked decision: A team proposes removing its second application instance, but the service must tolerate one instance failing. Compare savings against the availability requirement and test alternatives. The stated requirement must be preserved. Rightsizing waste may reduce cost without removing necessary redundancy.
distinctions: Reliability and security are different requirements even when one failure affects both.
Cost optimization does not mean choosing the lowest hourly price regardless of service requirements.

title: Separate CAF readiness from the seven migration strategies
explanation:
Migration requires business and operational readiness as well as data movement. The Cloud Adoption Framework considers business, people, governance, platform, security and operations perspectives. Workload strategies answer a different question. Retire removes an unneeded workload; retain leaves it in place for now. Rehost moves with limited redesign; replatform makes selected platform changes; refactor or re-architect changes the application more deeply. Repurchase replaces a product, often with SaaS. Relocate moves a compatible infrastructure environment without redesigning every application to the same degree. A portfolio can mix strategies. Inventory identity, data, network, licensing and operational dependencies before deciding. Define cutover, application validation and rollback; a copy finishing does not establish a successful business transition.

CAF perspectives describe capabilities and ownership, not server-copy commands. A rehost can be an intermediate stage before later modernization.

Worked decision: A legacy application has a three-month exit deadline and no tested redesign. Assess dependencies and a feasible rehost or replatform path while planning later modernization. The strategy must fit the deadline, dependencies and risk. Modernization and physical exit need not occur in one untested change.
distinctions: CAF perspectives describe capabilities and ownership, not server-copy commands.
A rehost can be an intermediate stage before later modernization.

title: Build a comparable TCO and rightsizing argument
explanation:
Total cost of ownership compares complete operating models over a stated period. Local costs can include equipment, facilities, power, maintenance, licenses, administration and refresh cycles. Cloud costs can include compute duration, storage capacity and requests, transfer, support, licenses, migration and operations. An omitted category is not necessarily a zero cost. Rightsizing uses utilization and performance evidence to select appropriate capacity rather than shrinking every instance. Check licensing rights before assuming bring-your-own-license portability. A fair model uses similar availability, recovery, growth and utilization assumptions. Variable consumption provides flexibility but needs monitoring and an owner who can act. Estimates should show uncertainty and be updated with measured usage after migration instead of being treated as guarantees.

A unit price is not the whole workload bill. Rightsizing must preserve performance and service requirements.

Worked decision: A proposal compares five years of redundant local infrastructure with one cloud VM's monthly price. Normalize period, resilience, licensing, transfer, storage and operations assumptions. The proposed designs and time periods are not comparable. Cost decisions require explicit assumptions about equivalent outcomes.

Rightsizing must preserve performance and service requirements.

title: Distinguish Regions, zones, edge locations and service scope
explanation:
A Region is a geographic AWS area containing multiple Availability Zones. A zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with independent infrastructure. Multi-zone design targets a zone failure, but the application must use redundant components and manage state correctly. Edge locations support particular edge services nearer users; they are not interchangeable with full Regions or universal database replicas. Service scope varies: do not assume every resource is copied everywhere. Multi-Region designs may address latency, disaster recovery or residency, but introduce replication, consistency, failover testing and cost choices. A second Region does not replace backups. DNS can direct clients to an endpoint but does not make application data current or validate every dependency behind that endpoint.

Multi-zone and multi-Region designs address different failure scopes. An edge cache does not replace its authoritative origin or every database function.

Worked decision: A cacheable static site is slow for distant users while its authoritative content remains in one Region. Evaluate edge content delivery with explicit cache freshness and origin behavior. An edge service can reduce delivery distance for suitable content; freshness and origin availability remain design responsibilities.

title: Separate billing discounts, interruption risk and capacity assurance
explanation:
On-Demand suits compute needing flexibility without a long usage commitment. Savings Plans and Reserved Instance options can suit predictable eligible use, but scope and flexibility differ. Spot uses spare capacity that can be interrupted, so applications need checkpoints, safe retry or replacement behavior. A discount commitment and capacity assurance are distinct dimensions. Savings Plans do not themselves reserve capacity; appropriate Capacity Reservations address specified capacity needs. Dedicated Hosts and Dedicated Instances concern tenancy or placement requirements that can involve compliance and licensing. Check current service terms rather than memorizing a universal discount. Include storage, transfer, idle capacity and fallback in the workload estimate. A purchase option is not a performance tier or a substitute for secure, recoverable application design.

A commitment discount does not universally guarantee capacity. Spot suitability requires application tolerance of interruption.

Worked decision: A batch job can checkpoint and safely restart after interruptions. Evaluate Spot with tested checkpoint, retry and fallback behavior. Restartability is useful evidence, but lost work and fallback costs must be included in the decision.
distinctions: A commitment discount does not universally guarantee capacity.
Spot suitability requires application tolerance of interruption.

title: Separate ECS/EKS orchestration from Fargate compute
explanation:
Containers package applications and dependencies but still require compute, networking, identity, storage and operations. ECS is AWS-native container orchestration; EKS provides managed Kubernetes capabilities. Choosing orchestration is different from selecting where containers run. EC2-based capacity leaves worker-instance administration with the customer. Fargate supplies serverless compute for supported ECS and EKS workloads, reducing worker-server provisioning and maintenance. It does not remove responsibility for images, permissions, application vulnerabilities, exposed services or data. Container execution also differs from Lambda's function model. Choose from ecosystem requirements, runtime constraints, control, scaling and cost. Diagnose image, scheduling, resource, identity and network failures separately rather than treating every error as an undifferentiated container fault.

ECS/EKS describe orchestration; Fargate describes a compute option. Serverless still has limits and application operating responsibilities.

Worked decision: A compatible workload requires Kubernetes APIs but aims to reduce worker-node administration. Evaluate EKS with supported serverless compute and check its constraints. The orchestration ecosystem and compute-management preference are separate design decisions.
distinctions: ECS/EKS describe orchestration; Fargate describes a compute option.
Serverless still has limits and application operating responsibilities.

title: Choose relational, key-value and cache services from access patterns
explanation:
Begin database selection with data model, access patterns, consistency, availability, operations and scale. RDS supplies managed relational options; Aurora is a relational engine family compatible with particular ecosystems. DynamoDB supplies managed key-value/document capabilities rather than a universal replacement for relational joins. ElastiCache offers in-memory caching capabilities that can reduce repeated work. A cache needs expiry, invalidation and failure behavior, and is not automatically the authoritative durable record. Databases hosted on EC2 retain more guest and database administration than suitable managed services. Managed infrastructure does not automatically optimize queries, schema, authorization or recovery choices. Evaluate realistic reads and writes and test restoration before concluding that the design meets the workload. A service described as fast can still be unsuitable for a required query pattern.

Relational and key-value models fit different access patterns. Caching does not replace authoritative storage or recovery.

Worked decision: An application repeatedly reads an expensive result that may be one minute stale. Evaluate a cache with explicit expiry and invalidation. Caching can reduce repeated reads, but the design must define staleness and source-of-truth behavior.
distinctions: Relational and key-value models fit different access patterns.
Caching does not replace authoritative storage or recovery.

title: Validate schema, data and applications during database migration
explanation:
Database migration has separate schema, transfer, application and cutover concerns. DMS supports suitable migration and replication workflows. Schema Conversion Tool helps assess or convert supported schema and code differences for applicable paths. Neither establishes that the application will behave correctly on a new engine. Heterogeneous migrations can encounter unsupported procedures, data types, collation, query behavior and tools. Inventory those dependencies; test conversion; compare data; measure lag during ongoing replication; and define when writes change over. Identify the cutover authority, new endpoint discovery and rollback triggers. Protect credentials and transferred data. Copy success is only one acceptance signal: appropriate data comparisons, application tests, performance and backup/restore behavior also need evidence. Decide how changes made after cutover would affect a potential rollback.

Schema conversion and data movement are distinct tasks. Migration success must be expressed in data and application terms.

Worked decision: A database copy completes, but the application relies on procedures unsupported by the destination. Assess conversion gaps and test application behavior before cutover. Data arrival does not resolve incompatible schema or application semantics.

Migration success must be expressed in data and application terms.

title: Match S3, EBS, EFS and FSx to storage interfaces
explanation:
Object, block and file storage have different interfaces. S3 stores objects in buckets for workloads such as media, archives and data lakes. EBS supplies block volumes for supported EC2 uses; a filesystem placed on a volume does not automatically become a general multi-client file service. EFS offers managed elastic file storage for suitable shared Linux workloads. FSx provides managed filesystems for particular compatibility and performance needs, including supported Windows and specialized filesystem requirements. Identify the client protocol, sharing pattern, update semantics and recovery target before selecting. Availability, durability, latency, throughput, retention and backup are separate concerns. A mounted path or familiar service label does not prove equivalent semantics. Managed storage can still be made unavailable by customer configuration, application failure or authorized deletion.

An object API is not a general block device. Shared filesystems must match client protocols and concurrency needs.

Worked decision: Several compatible Linux instances need read/write access to one shared filesystem. Evaluate EFS or another appropriate shared-file design. The required interface and sharing semantics narrow the choice; application testing is still necessary.

Shared filesystems must match client protocols and concurrency needs.

title: Balance S3 class retrieval behavior with lifecycle and hybrid access
explanation:
S3 storage classes address differing access and resilience patterns. Storage-byte price is only one variable: retrieval delay, retrieval requests, minimum storage duration and related charges can matter. Some archival options require data retrieval before use. Lifecycle rules can transition or expire eligible objects, but should follow reviewed retention and recovery requirements. Versioning, replication, backups and immutability address overlapping but different risks. Storage Gateway supports particular hybrid storage access patterns; the appropriate gateway depends on the application interface and workflow. Do not assume every gateway preserves every filesystem feature, or that an uploaded object is a tested recovery copy. Account for loss of connectivity, cache behavior, encryption, permissions and transfer time. A cheaper class can be a poor fit when the business requires immediate access.

Retrieval time and charges must be assessed with storage cost. A lifecycle transition is not a universal backup strategy.

Worked decision: An archive is rarely read, but one subset must be available immediately during investigations. Separate access requirements and choose appropriate tiers and retention. The access deadline is a functional requirement; infrequent access does not always imply delayed retrieval is acceptable.
distinctions: Retrieval time and charges must be assessed with storage cost.
A lifecycle transition is not a universal backup strategy.

title: Trace stateful security groups and stateless network ACLs
explanation:
Security groups apply supported stateful traffic rules to associated resources. Network ACLs apply stateless filtering at a subnet boundary. Stateful connection tracking changes how response traffic is handled; stateless filtering requires considering the necessary request and return directions explicitly. Neither mechanism creates a route, starts a listener or grants application authorization. Trace the source, destination, service port, routes, applicable controls and response path. Avoid opening all traffic as the default repair; define a narrow test and retain the original configuration. Rule capabilities and processing differ between security groups and ACLs, so do not transfer assumptions blindly. Even a successful TCP connection can be followed by application authorization failure. Diagnose the boundary with evidence rather than using a single successful ping to establish complete readiness.

Security groups are stateful while network ACLs are stateless. A traffic permission does not create routing or application readiness.

Worked decision: Responses disappear after a subnet ACL change, although requests enter the subnet. Review stateless request and required return-path rules. A stateless boundary may need explicit return allowances in addition to a correct route and other controls.

A traffic permission does not create routing or application readiness.

title: Separate outbound NAT from private service endpoints
explanation:
A private workload may need outbound updates without unsolicited inbound access. NAT can support suitable outbound IPv4 translation patterns, but is not a universal firewall or identity control. Internet gateways, routes and address configuration have different functions. VPC endpoints supply supported private connectivity to specific services without the same internet route; endpoint types and service support differ. Gateway and interface endpoints are not interchangeable. Review DNS, routing, security controls, endpoint policies and service authorization. A caller using a private network can still lack permission to read the data. Choose by destination, address family and required service path rather than adding NAT automatically. Availability and cost depend on traffic and architecture, so record failure behavior and billing implications alongside the connectivity diagram.

NAT translates addresses; it does not authorize service actions. A private endpoint is service-specific and still needs correct configuration.

Worked decision: A private application must access a supported AWS service without an ordinary internet egress path. Evaluate the correct VPC endpoint with its policy, DNS and routing requirements. An endpoint can fit the path requirement, while authorization and service support still need validation.

A private endpoint is service-specific and still needs correct configuration.

title: Place DNS, content delivery and private links in different layers
explanation:
Route 53 supplies DNS and related routing capabilities. Resolution does not replicate application data or establish that a selected target is healthy. CloudFront delivers supported content through edge locations using configured origins and cache behavior. It can improve delivery, but freshness, origin protection and authentication still require design. Site-to-site VPN supports encrypted tunnels over an underlying transport. Direct Connect supplies dedicated connectivity options; dedicated connectivity alone does not establish every required end-to-end encryption property. Compare bandwidth, routing, resilience, provider dependencies and confidentiality requirements. Failure at DNS, cache, route, target health or application authorization can look similar to a user while producing different evidence. A complete request-path diagram should identify these stages and trust boundaries rather than collapsing all four capabilities into a generic cloud connection.

DNS resolution and content delivery have different functions. Dedicated connectivity and encryption are separate requirements.

title: Separate analytics ingestion, integration, query and warehousing
explanation:
Analytics pipelines may collect, store, transform, catalog and query data. Athena supports suitable SQL queries over S3 data without customer-managed query servers. Glue provides data integration and catalog capabilities rather than being another name for an application database. Redshift provides data-warehouse capabilities for appropriate analysis workloads. Kinesis services address supported streaming workflows where arrival rates and processing delay matter. Choose from freshness, format, schema, permissions, scale and cost requirements. Serverless queries still consume resources, and scanned data can affect charges. Partitioning and file formats may change performance and cost. Validate that transformations preserve the intended meaning, and define privacy, retention and permitted use before moving sensitive data. A successful pipeline run is not proof that its output is correct or authorized for every downstream consumer.

Data preparation/cataloging and final query interfaces are distinct. Batch analysis and streaming can have different freshness targets.

Worked decision: A team occasionally queries historical files that already reside in S3. Evaluate Athena with suitable formats, permissions and scan-cost assumptions. The existing data location and intermittent query pattern are useful service-selection evidence.

title: Distinguish specialized AI, model workflows and foundation-model access
explanation:
Select an AI capability from a concrete task and approved data use. Specialized managed services can support tasks such as speech, text or image analysis without requiring a complete customer-built model workflow. SageMaker AI supports machine-learning development and deployment workflows. Bedrock provides managed access to supported foundation models and related capabilities. These differ in control, expertise, tuning, integration and governance. Generated output is not evidence of factual truth or authorization. Review error modes, human oversight, privacy, retention, regional/service availability and actual usage cost. Use approved non-sensitive evaluation data, known expected outcomes and recorded failure cases. A managed service does not make confidential content appropriate for unrestricted upload or turn a model's suggested command into an approved operational action.

A specialized prediction API differs from a model-development platform. Generative output needs validation rather than trust in confident wording.

title: Design SQS, SNS and EventBridge with retries and idempotency
explanation:
SQS supports queued work consumed by workers. SNS supports publish/subscribe notifications to supported subscribers. EventBridge routes supported events according to configured rules and integrations. These are distinct patterns even when one architecture uses all three. Delivery, order, retention and retry behavior depend on configuration, so do not assume a business action executes exactly once because one visible message arrived. An idempotent operation prevents a repeated attempt from creating a duplicate business effect such as a second charge. Handle failure destinations and poison messages deliberately. Monitor backlog, age and errors; an empty queue alone does not prove every intended request was accepted and completed. Test crashes between application state changes and acknowledgements, including recovery when the worker cannot tell whether a previous action finished.

A queue buffers work; pub/sub distributes notifications. Delivery behavior does not automatically make business actions idempotent.

Worked decision: A worker can crash after charging a customer but before acknowledging its message. Use business-level idempotency and tested retry behavior. The failure occurs between state change and acknowledgement, requiring duplicate-effect protection.

title: Correlate CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Config and detection findings
explanation:
Who changed a resource is a different question from why an application is slow. CloudTrail records supported account activity for audit and investigation. CloudWatch gathers operational telemetry such as metrics and logs and can drive configured alarms. Config tracks supported configuration state and changes and evaluates configured rules. GuardDuty detects suspicious activity from supported sources; a finding is a lead rather than complete attribution. Supported Security Hub capabilities can aggregate and prioritize relevant security information. Correlate identity, time, resource and context, and protect records from unauthorized changes. A compliant configuration check does not prove application performance, while a normal CPU graph does not prove a permission change was authorized. Collection scope, region, retention and access must be configured before an incident if the evidence is to be available afterward.

Metrics, account activity and configuration history answer different questions. Detection findings need investigation and corroboration.

title: Separate SCP permission guardrails from IAM grants
explanation:
Organizations structures accounts and supported organization-level management. Organizational units group accounts for governance. An SCP constrains the maximum permissions available to affected account identities; it does not grant an IAM identity permission by itself. Actual authorization still depends on relevant identity/resource policies, trust and applicable explicit denies. Thus a permissive SCP can coexist with a missing IAM grant, while a broad IAM grant can be limited by an applicable SCP. Consolidated billing and cost allocation are separate organizational capabilities. Account boundaries should reflect ownership, environments, security and operations, not convenience of a shared administrator. Restrictive policy changes can block critical operations across accounts, so test scope and preserve approved recovery access. Do not assume an SCP has identical effects on every possible outside principal, management-account identity or resource policy.

An SCP sets guardrails rather than granting permissions. Billing organization and workload authorization are distinct concerns.

Worked decision: A developer has an IAM grant but an applicable organization policy denies the action. Investigate the guardrail and use the approved exception/change process. An applicable deny can constrain a grant. Changes must follow scoped authorization and governance.

A support response target is not a promise that the application will recover within that period. AWS Health provides relevant service-event/account information where available; Trusted Advisor provides supported checks and recommendations. Neither replaces the workload owner's incident, recovery and communication procedures. Before an incident, record who can open cases, how severity is determined, what redacted evidence is useful and how internal escalation runs in parallel. title: Compare availability sets, zones and regional recovery
explanation:

Availability sets let Azure account for fault and update domains for appropriate VM deployments; this differs from distributing across physically separate availability zones. Zones exist in supported regions and have independent infrastructure. The application must use redundant components and manage traffic and state correctly to benefit. Creating a zone label does not make an ordinary single VM and its data automatically fail over. Regional disaster recovery introduces separate replication, endpoint, identity, testing and possible data-loss questions. Service support and preview capabilities change, so inspect the exact resource, region, disk and network requirements before assuming a failover behavior. Backups remain necessary alongside live redundancy. Compare the service objective with supported options and prove recovery with a test rather than interpreting two diagram symbols as resilience.

An availability set and a multi-zone design target different placement risks. Redundancy does not automatically make application state recoverable.

explanation:

The fleet still needs suitable images, health signals, networking, permissions, storage and an application that tolerates instance replacement and distribution. Azure Virtual Desktop addresses supported remote desktop and application-delivery experiences. Host pools, identity, profiles, access and licensing create different design concerns from a public web fleet. Azure VMs provide infrastructure-level control; App Service, container services and Functions supply other hosting choices with different responsibility boundaries. Identify whether the requirement is remote user desktops, a VM application fleet or managed runtime execution before selecting. explanation:

A public IP is not mandatory for every VM and should not be added merely for convenience. Guest patching, applications and access configuration remain relevant customer responsibilities. Disk choice, backup and recovery-key handling affect recovery. VM size, storage performance and network limits can produce different bottlenecks: increasing CPU does not automatically cure slow storage. A gateway or circuit is only one part of the complete path: on-premises devices, DNS and application endpoints may still fail. explanation:

They are not interchangeable interfaces merely because they can appear in a storage account. Blob tiers address differing access patterns and retention costs. title: Compare local, zonal and geo-redundancy with secondary read access
explanation:

title: Test Conditional Access, MFA and recovery as a policy system
explanation:
Conditional Access evaluates supported identity and contextual signals against configured access policy. Signals and controls depend on product features, licensing and configuration. A policy may require stronger authentication or restrict access based on context. MFA uses different factor categories; two knowledge secrets do not become MFA because two prompts appear. Passwordless methods require registration, recovery and lifecycle controls despite avoiding a reusable password. SSO reduces repeated sign-in interactions across integrated apps; it does not make their authorizations identical. Before broad enforcement, test intended users, applications, devices, exceptions, logging and recovery access. An apparently strong rule can lock out administrators or break a legitimate workload when assumptions are wrong. Staged testing should include allowed, denied and recovery paths, not only a successful administrator sign-in.

Authentication requirements and application permissions are separate. SSO reduces repeated sign-in rather than merging every app's permissions.

Worked decision: A proposed compliant-device policy includes the organization's only recovery administrator. Test scope and an approved recovery-access design before enforcement. Security controls must remain operable during failure and recovery as well as normal work.
distinctions: Authentication requirements and application permissions are separate.
SSO reduces repeated sign-in rather than merging every app's permissions.

title: Compute effective resource access from principal, role and scope
explanation:
An Azure RBAC assignment combines principal, role definition and scope. Principals include users, groups, service principals and managed identities. Roles define permitted actions; scopes range from higher management levels to particular resources. Inherited assignments can affect many descendants, so inspect effective access rather than one visible resource setting. Management-plane actions and data actions are not always interchangeable; managing a storage account does not establish every form of data access. Entra directory roles govern a different administrative surface from Azure resource roles. Managed identities can avoid embedding application credentials, but still need appropriate authorization. Diagnose which identity made which request against which target, and consider inherited assignments and applicable restrictions. Granting Owner everywhere hides the actual missing permission and expands risk instead of providing a scoped repair.

Role definition and assignment scope jointly determine reach. Resource roles and directory roles govern different surfaces.

Worked decision: A service can manage a resource group but should read data only from one storage target. Determine required data actions and grant narrow suitable access. Least privilege requires distinguishing actions, data access and scope.

Resource roles and directory roles govern different surfaces.

title: Use Zero Trust principles with posture and workload protection
explanation:
Zero Trust is an architectural approach rather than one product switch. Explicit verification evaluates relevant evidence; least privilege limits permission and duration; assuming breach encourages segmentation, observation and containment. Defense in depth layers complementary controls. Defender for Cloud offers supported posture and workload-protection capabilities, but a dashboard does not automatically secure or certify every workload. Customers must select scope, review entitlements, establish ownership and investigate findings. A recommendation is not identical to an incident, and neither can establish the complete application risk alone. Prioritize findings using exposure, business impact and supporting evidence. A cleared recommendation does not show every application threat is removed. Map identity, platform, network, application and data controls to requirements, then test whether intended boundaries hold rather than trusting a green summary.

Zero Trust guides decisions across systems; it is not a universal product guarantee. Posture recommendations and incident signals require different interpretation.

Worked decision: A team wants to remove application permissions because its security dashboard is green. Retain scoped application controls and use dashboard evidence as a complementary layer. Independent controls and verification remain necessary even with monitoring products.

Posture recommendations and incident signals require different interpretation.

title: Separate configuration policy, locks and data governance
explanation:
Azure Policy evaluates supported resource configurations and can enforce or remediate applicable requirements. It differs from granting a principal permission to act. Resource locks help protect against accidental deletion or modification according to type; authorized users may be able to remove them. They do not create a recoverable copy. Purview supplies supported data discovery, governance and compliance-related capabilities, whose exact scope and licensing must be checked for the task. A tag can label a resource but does not by itself enforce allowed locations or verify classification. Identify what is controlled: the caller's actions, permitted resource configuration, a destructive operation or the discovery/classification of data. Several mechanisms may be needed together, with ownership and an exception process. Recovery, privacy obligations and data retention still require their own evidence.

RBAC controls actions; Policy evaluates supported configuration requirements. A lock helps prevent changes but is not a backup.

title: Connect declarative deployment with management beyond Azure
explanation:
Resource Manager is Azure's deployment and management layer. Supported portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDK and API operations pass through management controls and authorization. ARM templates and Bicep describe desired infrastructure declaratively; Bicep is an authoring language using ARM deployment capabilities. Version parameters, dependencies and outputs while keeping secrets out of source. A syntax-valid or successful resource deployment does not prove application readiness. Arc extends supported management and governance capabilities to selected resources outside Azure; it does not physically move an on-premises server into a region or make every external system a VM. Separate infrastructure definitions, connected-resource management and application operations. Plan drift detection, scoped credentials, controlled changes, testing and recovery for automated deployments, and check onboarding/support requirements before connecting external resources.

Desired-state infrastructure and application health require different evidence. Arc extends management rather than automatically migrating workloads.

title: Correlate metrics, logs, traces, service health and recommendations
explanation:
Monitor supplies supported telemetry collection, analysis and response. Metrics summarize measurements over time; logs record events that can be queried; application tracing follows requests and dependencies. Log Analytics supports log queries, while Application Insights supplies supported application diagnostics within this ecosystem. Service Health provides personalized information about relevant service issues and maintenance; public status information has a different scope. Advisor recommendations are not the same as a confirmed incident or current workload symptom. A slow app may involve code, downstream services, saturation, network behavior or provider issues. Correlate timestamps, resource scope and request evidence before selecting a repair. Alerts need actionable thresholds and response ownership. Retention, collection and sampling settings determine which evidence survives, so decide those before an incident rather than expecting absent records to be reconstructed.

Telemetry, service events and recommendations answer different questions. An alert needs an owner and a response process.

title: Connect estimates, actual spending, tags and cost-response ownership
explanation:
Pricing estimates depend on planned configuration and consumption assumptions. Actual spending can differ through usage, retention, transfer, service choices and pricing circumstances. Cost Management supports investigation of cost and usage, while budgets can notify responsible people about configured thresholds. An alert alone does not universally stop resources or cap charges. Define who investigates a spike and who may authorize rightsizing, schedule changes or retention adjustments. Tags can aid attribution, but they need consistency and applicable reporting support; shared and untagged costs may need another allocation method. Do not disrupt production merely because spending rises: connect cost to service requirements and business outcomes. Estimates, historical reports, forecasts and enforcement actions are distinct parts of the workflow. Automated actions need a scoped design, tests and recovery just as other operational changes do.

A budget notification is not a universal spending stop. Low price does not remove availability and business requirements.

title: Turn uncertain demand into a capacity decision
explanation: Cloud value begins with a business constraint rather than a promise that every bill becomes smaller. Buying equipment requires estimating peak demand before demand is known. Metered resources let a team begin smaller and adjust capacity as evidence arrives. Elasticity means matching provisioned capacity to changing demand; scalability means an architecture can handle growth. A scalable application that never scales down can still waste money. Agility concerns the time and effort needed to experiment and deliver changes. Global infrastructure can shorten deployment distance to customers, but the application still needs routing and data placement. Economies of scale describe provider purchasing and operating advantages; they do not remove customer charges. Evaluate migration using utilization, variable charges, staffing and recovery requirements. The useful outcome is a defensible decision about speed, risk and total cost.

title: Assign security controls at the service boundary
explanation: Shared responsibility separates protection of provider infrastructure from protection of a customer workload. On EC2, the customer normally maintains the guest operating system, applications, identities and network rules. Moving to a managed database changes who maintains the underlying host and database platform, but customers still choose permissions, data handling and supported configuration. With S3, customers do not patch a storage server; they must control object access and choose suitable protection settings. Responsibility follows the actual service and configuration. A compliance report for AWS infrastructure cannot establish that an application uses least privilege or that recovery works. During a review, name the asset, control owner and evidence for each control. Using a managed service does not remove all customer security tasks. Review remaining identity and data decisions when determining what operational work transferred.

Provider reports do not validate customer access policies.

title: Trace an IAM request through effective permissions
explanation: An AWS access decision evaluates a principal, action, resource and request context. Authentication establishes who makes a request; authorization determines whether it is permitted. Identity policies grant actions to users and roles, while resource policies grant access at supported resources. An explicit deny in an applicable policy overrides an allow. Permissions boundaries and service control policies constrain permissions rather than granting application access themselves. For a simple identity-policy request subject to a boundary and SCP, the action must survive each constraint. Resource-policy grants have additional principal-specific evaluation rules, so avoid treating every real request as a universal intersection. Role trust policies determine who may assume a role; permission policies govern what an assumed session may do. Temporary credentials still carry permissions and expiration. Diagnose access using the actual principal and conditions, including region, tags and MFA.
distinctions: Trust controls role assumption; permissions control later actions.
Boundaries and SCPs limit access without independently granting it.

title: Separate account recovery from daily administration
explanation: The AWS account root user is a highly privileged identity associated with the account sign-in email. Protect root credentials and reserve them for tasks requiring that privilege. Organize daily human access through federation and roles with multifactor authentication and least privilege. Do not assume every administrative task requires root because an ordinary user lacks permission. Review the current documented root-only task list first. Certain account-setting changes and recovery operations require exceptional privileges. Supported centralized root access can handle selected privileged tasks for organization member accounts and remove standing root credentials, so older advice to maintain a root password everywhere is incomplete. Protect recovery contact channels and define how authorized staff obtain emergency access. Avoid root keys for routine automation. Record evidence and return to ordinary roles after exceptional tasks.

title: Distinguish keys, certificates and compliance evidence
explanation: Encryption needs controlled access to key material. AWS KMS provides managed cryptographic keys and integrations with AWS services; object access does not automatically imply permission to decrypt content. Key policies and supported authorization controls govern KMS use. Envelope encryption protects data with a data key and protects that key with a higher-level key, avoiding centralized encryption of every large payload. AWS CloudHSM addresses dedicated hardware security module requirements with greater customer control and additional administration. AWS Certificate Manager handles supported TLS certificate provisioning and lifecycle tasks rather than general application-secret storage. Compliance evidence is separate: AWS Artifact supplies provider reports and agreements, while customers evaluate their own workload obligations. Encryption is one control rather than a complete compliance program. Recovery planning must include key availability because retained ciphertext without usable authorized keys may not be recoverable.

Provider reports and workload encryption answer different questions.

title: Rotate secrets as a coordinated workflow
explanation: An application secret is a credential or token used to authenticate to another system. Hard-coded database passwords spread into repositories, build logs and packages. AWS Secrets Manager stores and retrieves secrets and supports configured rotation workflows. Applications can retrieve an authorized value at runtime rather than embedding it in source. Rotation must coordinate the store with the database or external system accepting the credential. Changing a stored string does not prove the target accepts it. Design for retrieval errors, appropriate caching and supported version transitions. Restrict secret retrieval separately from metadata administration. KMS manages encryption keys, while Secrets Manager manages application-secret lifecycles. IAM roles are preferable to stored permanent AWS keys for supported workloads. Diagnostic records should identify versions and error categories without revealing values. Validate that rotation preserves application connectivity and removes unintended continuing use of obsolete credentials.

Rotation must update the accepting system consistently.

title: Read deployment intent across interfaces
explanation: The AWS console, CLI and SDKs are interfaces to service operations. A graphical console does not create a different class of resource from an API request. CLI commands support repeatable operator tasks; SDKs integrate requests into application code. CloudShell provides a browser command environment using the signed-in identity, so commands still need permissions and can have real effects. Infrastructure as code records intended resources in a reviewable definition. CloudFormation manages stacks from templates with supported dependency and change workflows. A template alone does not prove deployment succeeded: inspect operation results and resulting resources. Choosing an interface is separate from choosing cloud-only or hybrid placement. Outposts places supported AWS infrastructure at a customer location, while a VPN provides connectivity. For study, interpreting a definition and predicting its resources does not require executing a create command.

Templates express intent; operation results establish state.

title: Estimate charges by usage dimension
explanation: AWS prices depend on service, region, configuration and measured usage. Compute can involve execution time, capacity or requests; storage can involve capacity, operations, retrieval and transfer. Identify each unit being multiplied and the workload behavior changing its quantity. Committed-use discounts can help predictable eligible usage but introduce risk if demand shrinks. Spot trades lower prices for interruption exposure and suits work designed to retry or checkpoint. Dedicated placement addresses tenancy requirements and is not automatically the cheapest choice. Transfer treatment depends on service and path, so avoid assuming all transfer is free. A calculator predicts charges from assumptions rather than enforcing a spending ceiling. Revisit current rates and free-offer eligibility before purchase. Compare alternatives under the same utilization and recovery requirements; a cheaper hourly resource can become expensive when retrieval or operational costs are added.

title: Match EC2 family to the bottleneck
explanation: An EC2 type combines family, generation and size with particular compute, memory, storage and networking capabilities. General-purpose families balance resources. Compute-optimized choices target processor-intensive work; memory-optimized choices fit large working sets. Storage-optimized choices address demanding local storage patterns, and accelerated computing supplies specialized hardware such as GPUs. Choosing the largest type without locating the bottleneck can increase cost without improving results. Processor architecture and software compatibility also matter: an image built for one architecture cannot be assumed to run on another. Instance-store data follows documented instance-lifecycle behavior, while EBS provides separately managed block storage. Check persistence before stopping or terminating a workload. Family choice is independent of purchase arrangement. First identify a suitable resource configuration, then compare eligible commitments, On-Demand and interruption-tolerant Spot arrangements for that configuration.

title: Check limits before relying on elasticity
explanation: Flexible cloud capacity remains subject to service quotas and actual availability. Quotas define allowed quantities or request rates within documented scopes, often per account and Region. Some are adjustable through requests and others are fixed. A submitted increase is not an applied increase, and an approved quota does not guarantee a particular instance type is available in a selected zone. Inspect the applied account value rather than assuming the published default applies, especially for new accounts. Check quotas before a launch and monitor utilization and throttling. A budget alarm answers a financial question and does not increase a limit. Another IAM allow cannot fix an exhausted quota. Diagnose failures by category: permission denial, quota exhaustion, throttling, unsupported region or unavailable capacity. Retry with appropriate backoff rather than repeatedly issuing requests without identifying the failure.

title: Choose recovery using RPO and RTO
explanation: Recovery point objective describes acceptable data loss measured in time. Recovery time objective describes acceptable restoration duration. Neither is guaranteed because a backup exists. Backup and restore can be economical but require provisioning and restoration work. Pilot light keeps essential components ready while other capacity is activated during recovery. Warm standby maintains a reduced functioning environment that can scale. Multi-site active/active serves traffic across locations with added replication, routing and consistency complexity. These strategies are tradeoffs rather than fixed guaranteed times. Regional availability and regional disaster recovery address different failure boundaries. Replication may copy corruption or accidental deletion, so retained independent recovery points matter. AWS Backup centralizes supported backup management; Elastic Disaster Recovery supports server recovery workflows. A restore exercise should validate the application, permissions and dependencies rather than merely confirm that a disk appeared.
distinctions: RPO measures data-loss tolerance; RTO measures restoration time.
Replication and independent recovery points address different failures.

title: Choose cloud placement from the constraint
explanation: Cloud services expose computing capabilities through managed abstractions, commonly with usage-based charging. Public cloud serves customers through provider-operated environments; public does not require exposing every application publicly. Private cloud is dedicated to an organization and requires operating its underlying environment or arranging that operation. Hybrid design connects on-premises or private resources with public services to meet constraints such as latency, data placement or migration sequencing. Two unrelated websites do not establish hybrid integration. Consumption pricing depends on measured dimensions, so stopping compute can leave disks and networking billable. Serverless reduces server administration and supports event-based execution while retaining provider infrastructure, limits and customer duties. Choose the model from the business requirement and describe connectivity, identity and operating ownership. Existing hardware can remain useful during transition without forcing every new application into the same placement.
distinctions: Public cloud can host privately reachable workloads.
Hybrid means integrated environments rather than merely two accounts.

title: Make cloud benefits measurable
explanation: Cloud benefits require an architecture and operating process that deliver them. High availability reduces disruption through suitable redundancy and failover. Scalability increases capacity with demand; elasticity follows changing demand dynamically. Reliability includes consistent operation and recovery after failures. Predictability requires measurements and planning for performance and cost. Security features supply controls while customers still configure identities and data handling. Governance establishes organizational rules and checks. Manageability includes resource interfaces and automation as well as monitoring and controlled service changes. Turn each promised benefit into an acceptance criterion: a failure to tolerate, response-time target, budget threshold or required configuration. A single cloud VM is not automatically highly available. Testing should match the promised outcome; a cheaper price estimate cannot establish restore reliability. Consider dependencies because a redundant application can still depend on one fragile database.
distinctions: Redundancy needs functioning failover.
Cost and performance predictability need different measurements.

example.situation: A migrated app still uses one VM but is called highly available.
example.reasoning: Cloud location does not establish redundancy.
example.result: Define failure tolerance and design the required controls.

questions.explanation: Growth capacity does not prove recovery.

title: Choose platform responsibility deliberately
explanation: IaaS provides infrastructure such as VMs while customers manage guest operating systems and software. It suits OS-level requirements but retains patching work. PaaS provides a managed platform for applications or data services, reducing host administration while retaining application behavior and data responsibilities. SaaS supplies a finished application consumed by users. These models describe abstraction rather than quality rankings. A managed runtime may not support a required kernel driver; a VM may impose unnecessary maintenance for a supported web application. Solutions often combine service models. Authentication, authorization and sensible information handling remain relevant with SaaS. Identify the layer requiring customer control and choose an appropriate administrative burden. A web portal alone does not identify a model because all three can have portals. Document retained responsibilities rather than assuming a provider manages every layer of a service.
distinctions: OS control suggests IaaS; supported code without host management suggests PaaS.
SaaS retains customer identity and data duties.

example.reasoning: The workloads require different control layers.
example.result: Evaluate VMs for the legacy app and App Service for the website.

Classify a driver requirement, web API and employee email; state retained operating work.

questions.explanation: PaaS manages the supporting platform.

title: Separate placement from administrative scope
explanation: Azure physical placement and administrative scope are different concepts. A datacenter is a facility; availability zones separate supported locations within a Region. A Region is a geographic deployment area with service-specific capabilities. Some Regions form region pairs while others are nonpaired. Pairing does not automatically replicate every application or configure recovery. Sovereign environments such as Azure Government and Azure operated by 21Vianet have distinct eligibility, operations and service availability; verify actual regulatory requirements. The management hierarchy is management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources. A resource group can contain resources in different Regions; its metadata location does not dictate every resource location. Subscriptions provide important billing and access boundaries, and management groups organize governance across subscriptions. Scope affects inherited access and policy, while region selection affects placement. Verify the chosen service's supported locations and redundancy instead of relying solely on geographical labels.
distinctions: Resource-group location does not force contained resource locations.
Region pairs do not create automatic application failover.

example.situation: A team expects an automatic VM replica because its Region is paired.
example.reasoning: Pair association does not configure a recovery environment.
example.result: Design explicit service replication and recovery.

Only resources with zone redundancy can differ

questions.explanation: Sovereign environments have distinct constraints.

title: Diagnose delegation and private resolution
explanation: DNS supplies records clients use to locate services. Azure Public DNS hosts authoritative records but creating a zone does not register a domain. Delegation at the parent or registrar must direct public queries to the intended authoritative servers. An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address; CNAME aliases one name to another. Private DNS supports resolution in connected private networking scopes rather than publishing records to the internet. Virtual-network links support resolution within the relevant scope, while hybrid networks may need forwarding or Private Resolver. DNS does not authorize access, open a firewall or guarantee application health. If a private service resolves to a public address, inspect the resolver path and private-zone links before changing credentials. Separate authoritative hosting, recursive resolution and network reachability during diagnosis. A cached answer can persist until its applicable lifetime expires, so changing a record is not proof every client immediately sees it.
distinctions: Zone hosting and domain registration differ.
Resolution success does not prove network or application access.

example.situation: A private-endpoint client resolves the public address.
example.reasoning: The resolver may not see the private zone.
example.result: Check records, links and forwarding.

questions.explanation: Delegation determines authoritative hosting.

questions.explanation: Resolution does not prove transport or authorization.

title: Validate storage-account feature combinations
explanation: A storage account provides namespace and configuration boundaries for supported services. Standard general-purpose v2 supports common combinations of blobs, files, queues and tables. Specialized premium account kinds target workloads such as block blobs, file shares or page blobs. Account kind, performance, region and redundancy must be considered together; a capability available in one combination is not automatically available in every other. Blob access tiers describe access frequency and retrieval economics rather than replacing account performance categories. Hierarchical namespace enables supported Data Lake capabilities, while SMB and NFS requirements must be matched to the specific service and prerequisites. Queues store messages and tables hold structured NoSQL data; neither is a shared filesystem. Build a requirement matrix for interface, performance, redundancy and access pattern. Verify current feature support rather than assuming premium means every capability is included.
distinctions: Performance tier and blob access tier differ.
Specialized premium accounts do not universally support every standard service.

example.situation: A premium blob account is expected to supply queues and SMB shares.
example.reasoning: Specialized capabilities must be checked separately.
example.result: Choose supported account types for each requirement.

options: Access economics and performance categories differ

Premium automatically includes every blob access tier

title: Follow data discovery through governance
explanation: Purview data governance helps organizations discover, understand and manage data across their estate. Discovery identifies assets. Catalog context, business meaning, ownership and lineage help users decide what data to use and understand how it was produced. Classification and quality information support risk and trust decisions, but finding a sensitive column does not automatically revoke every user's access or encrypt its data. Governance also needs accountable owners and remediation workflows. Azure Policy evaluates resource configuration against organizational rules, while resource locks protect supported management operations. These tools complement a data catalog without being interchangeable. A useful workflow starts with a business question, finds the relevant asset, checks ownership, lineage and quality, then follows approved access processes. A catalog supplies understanding, not proof every record is correct or every protection is enforced. Capture evidence of remediation and periodically review ownership as business processes change.
distinctions: Classification informs decisions; enforcement requires applicable controls.
Policy checks resource rules; Purview supplies data governance context.

example.situation: Analysts find three revenue datasets with unclear ownership.
example.reasoning: They need lineage, ownership and quality context.
example.result: Identify the governed asset and approved access route.

Proof that all source data passed quality checks

title: Choose workforce or customer identity
explanation: A Microsoft Entra tenant is an identity boundary rather than a synonym for a subscription. One tenant can associate with multiple subscriptions, which retain resource access scopes. External ID supports people outside an organization. Workforce business-to-business collaboration lets approved external identities access organizational applications and resources under configured controls. Customer-facing applications can instead use an external tenant designed for customer identity experiences. These scenarios have different audiences and administration needs. Giving shoppers broad Azure roles is not a customer sign-in design. Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines allowed resource or application actions. Federation lets an identity provider participate without distributing an identical local password everywhere. Review invitations, consent, conditional access and least privilege for the supported configuration. Removing a subscription role differs from deleting an identity or changing an application's own authorization. Design offboarding for the access path actually used.
distinctions: Tenant identity and subscription scope differ.
Partner collaboration and customer identity target different audiences.

title: Interpret CLI and Bicep without deploying
explanation: Azure management tools use the signed-in identity and selected scope. Command lines do not bypass access checks. Read a command by separating service group, action and arguments. For example, az group list requests inventory, whereas az group create requests a change. Query arguments can shape displayed output without changing resources. Bicep declaratively describes resources and compiles into Resource Manager templates. A resource declaration identifies type, API version, name and properties; an existing declaration references a resource instead of requesting its creation. Parameters provide variable input and outputs expose selected results, so avoid secret outputs. Opening or compiling a file is different from submitting a deployment. A preview helps assess intent but does not guarantee every runtime outcome. Study exercises can annotate samples entirely on paper before any authorized cloud interaction. Deployed state requires separate evidence.
distinctions: Compilation does not deploy resources.
Output filtering differs from create/update/delete actions.

title: Read KQL inventory versus telemetry
explanation: Kusto Query Language pipelines filter, shape and summarize records. Resource Graph queries resource inventory using a supported KQL subset; Azure Monitor Logs queries ingested telemetry in workspaces. Similar syntax does not imply identical data. In Resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines' | project name, location, the filter matches type case-insensitively and project selects displayed columns. A summarize count() by location groups matching rows into regional counts. A limit caps returned rows rather than establishing total inventory. Missing results can reflect permissions, scope or ingestion delay instead of organizational absence. Read table and selected subscription or workspace before interpreting emptiness. Queries display available records rather than remediating misconfiguration. For study, calculate results from a small invented table without inspecting customer inventory. To report a total, verify both aggregation semantics and whether the authorized scope covers the intended population.
distinctions: Resource Graph inventories resources; Log Analytics queries collected telemetry.
Limited output is not necessarily total count.

example.reasoning: The cap limits output, not inventory.

title: Select specialized AI by input and output
explanation: AI-service questions often become clearer when the required input and output are explicit. Audio turned into text differs from text spoken aloud; translating language differs from detecting sentiment within the original text. A scanned form needs document extraction rather than merely a general image label. A conversational interface combines natural-language understanding with dialogue behavior, while a managed machine-learning platform supports building and operating custom models. Generative assistants are not interchangeable with deterministic database queries, and outputs still require validation for the task. Match the smallest supported capability before selecting a larger platform requiring training or additional engineering. Consider privacy, permissions, supported languages and output accuracy. The current Cloud Practitioner in-scope list names Amazon Q and SageMaker AI, and lists Amazon Quick in analytics. Older materials may use older branding. Service recognition does not establish that a resulting answer is accurate or appropriate for a business decision.
distinctions: Transcribe changes audio to text; Polly changes text to speech.
Textract extracts document fields; Rekognition analyzes image and video content.

example.reasoning: The directions of transformation differ.

title: Distinguish orchestration, approved products and operations
explanation: Service selection should begin with the required operational outcome. Provisioning a known environment is different from delivering approved products to teams, operating a fleet or tracing an individual request. CloudFormation records infrastructure definitions; Service Catalog distributes approved products; Systems Manager supports operational management of supported nodes and resources. A pipeline coordinates delivery stages while a build service runs build and test work. Traces show request paths and timing, whereas metrics summarize behavior and audit events record API activity. A recommendation tool does not automatically implement every recommendation. Inventory, assessment and enforcement are separate stages requiring appropriate permissions and verification. The catalog below adds commonly confused services that appear in foundational scenarios. Combine them only when the scenario requires their separate capabilities. For example, a reviewed product can be provisioned from a template, updated through a delivery pipeline and monitored after release. Naming all three is not proof the released system meets its requirements.
distinctions: Service Catalog distributes approved products; CloudFormation describes provisioning.
CodePipeline coordinates stages; CodeBuild runs build work.

title: Match preventive and detective security services
explanation: Security tools solve different parts of a control and investigation workflow. Preventive controls can filter traffic or constrain access, while detective tools identify suspicious behavior, vulnerable software or sensitive data. Findings aggregation helps prioritize work but does not replace the original evidence or automatically remove every risk. Investigation tools help analysts understand relationships and activity after a finding. Customer application sign-in differs from employee access to multiple AWS accounts, and directory integration differs from sharing an existing resource across accounts. Read the required action carefully before selecting a service: detect, investigate, aggregate, authenticate, filter or share. For a suspected compromise, retain relevant evidence, confirm the finding and apply authorized remediation; merely opening a dashboard does not establish containment. The reference distinguishes frequently confused services. Many workloads need several of them, but the best answer to a focused scenario is the capability directly meeting its stated requirement.
distinctions: GuardDuty detects threats; Inspector identifies supported workload vulnerabilities.
WAF filters application requests; Shield addresses DDoS protection.

title: Separate discovery, business case, migration and tracking
explanation: Migration planning involves several jobs that should not be confused. Application Discovery Service collects supported configuration, utilization and dependency information to understand existing workloads. Migration Evaluator uses assessment information to develop a business case and cost comparisons; an estimate is not an executed move. Application Migration Service, called AWS Transform MGN in current service-overview material, supports server rehosting workflows with replication, testing and cutover. The certification in-scope list can retain the older Application Migration Service label, so recognize both names. Migration Hub supports visibility and progress tracking across migration activities rather than replacing every underlying migration engine. DMS targets supported database movement and replication, while schema conversion addresses structural differences between engines. Begin with dependencies and business goals, group suitable migration waves, test before cutover and retain a rollback decision. A dashboard showing completion is insufficient if the application cannot authenticate or reach a dependency after relocation.

Migration Hub tracks progress; MGN performs supported server migration work.

title: Choose acceleration, transit or remote-access networking
explanation: A network scenario may concern application delivery, network interconnection or individual-user access. Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network and static anycast addressing to direct supported application traffic toward healthy endpoints. It is not a content cache. CloudFront is a content-delivery network with caching and supported edge processing, while Route 53 supplies DNS capabilities. Transit Gateway acts as a regional transit hub connecting supported VPC and on-premises attachments, reducing complex meshes; routing tables still determine which networks can communicate. Client VPN gives individual users supported remote-access VPN connectivity. Site-to-Site VPN instead connects networks through tunnels, and Direct Connect supplies dedicated connectivity arrangements rather than automatically encrypting all traffic. PrivateLink provides private access to supported services without requiring general routing access to an entire provider network. Choose the service from the endpoints and traffic requirement. Connectivity alone does not grant application permissions or remove firewall and route configuration duties.
distinctions: Global Accelerator improves supported traffic paths; CloudFront caches content.
Client VPN connects users; Site-to-Site VPN connects networks.

title: Separate procurement from detailed cost analysis
explanation: AWS Marketplace is a catalog for finding and obtaining third-party software, data and services through supported commercial arrangements. Listings can use different deployment and licensing models, so compare software fees, infrastructure charges, term, renewal and support responsibilities. Procurement through Marketplace does not transfer all seller-product security or operational work to AWS. Cost and Usage Reports provide detailed billing and usage records for analysis, commonly delivered to a customer-controlled S3 destination. They help break charges into usage types, operations and other supported dimensions; they are not instant enforcement controls. Cost Explorer supports interactive cost exploration, while Budgets supports configured cost or usage thresholds and supported notifications or actions. A report or dashboard can change as billing data is processed and finalized. Inspect timestamps and accounting assumptions before reconciling totals. Protect report data because usage details can reveal internal resource patterns. A purchase decision and later attribution of its charges are different workflows requiring different evidence.

A report is not a hard spending cap or an immediate final invoice.

example.reasoning: Procurement and cost attribution require separate capabilities.
